detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Surrey, 1894, low sun from the left, black shadow.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on a medium shot of <Subject 1>, bare-headed with his auburn hair blown wild, in the mustard-ochre tweed suit and round steel spectacles, his trousers dark with dew to the knee at the foot of the huge crusted lid, both hands already reaching out toward the glowing metal, heat haze rising off it around his fingers, the curved crusted hull towering many times his height and running out of the frame at both sides. The camera is on the pit floor at a standing man's eye, three long strides from him, a 35mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT onto the crust. At the first frame Ogilvy stands at the CENTRE of the frame from the gravel at the BOTTOM edge to the TOP third, his head a quarter of the frame's height. The shot is inside this place: A great raw crater on Horsell Common at sunrise in 1894: sloping walls of loose yellow sand and grey gravel, a charred rim ringed with flung heaps of spoil, splintered fir wood on the gravel floor, and lying half-buried across the pit a colossal cylinder thirty yards across, one long continuous hull running back deep into the sand. The camera pulls back from <Subject 1>'s outstretched hands, widening to show the whole crusted end of the cylinder above him as he snatches his hands back from the heat and shakes them, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 he turns and scrambles up the sand wall, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. <Subject 1>'s mouth is closed from 00:00 to 00:06 while he snatches his hands back from the heat and shakes them. By 00:07 the camera is pulling back through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
